title: Resolve a service's modules
goal: The service's go.mod and go.sum hold the modules its generated code needs, resolved from exactly the source STEGO captured.
notes: Decisions of 2026-10-28: Building runs from generated source to a signed image; the platform side (CI, manifests, platform requirements) is Delivering. A rebuild from the same inputs gives the same bytes; every build runs offline from a recorded module cache; the archetype pins the Go SDK; images are built only from a stego build and its record, on scratch; every image carries SPDX and CycloneDX SBOMs and a keyless cosign signature whose identity is the platform's pinned reusable workflow.

title: Start a service declaration
goal: The author has a declaration that STEGO already accepts, and a place to put fills.
notes: A scaffold is valid as written, because each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts. An archetype that can be meaningfully empty, such as rest-crud, needs none. One that cannot, such as rpc-service, supplies a minimal proto file. An author who does not want that content asks for an empty scaffold, and STEGO then names every setting they must supply before checking will accept the declaration.

title: Learn what may be declared
goal: The agent knows every field, setting and slot it may write, before it writes any of them.
notes: Its step reads Supplying's query Report what may be declared (ST-SUP-QRY01), a deliberate deviation from keeping queries inside their domain: what may be declared is the registry, which Supplying owns, and stego registry inspect reads it directly. A read changes no aggregate.

title: Check a declaration
goal: The author knows whether the declaration is acceptable, and the project is untouched either way.
notes: This use case relies on every invariant of the Declaration aggregate, which it applies rather than restates. Its own requirements say only how checking behaves: that it writes nothing, that it reports every fault, and that it happens once.

title: Repair a refused declaration
goal: The agent corrects the declaration from the refusal alone, with no person reading the message.
notes: This use case is why a refusal is data and not prose. STEGO's premise is that an agent writes the declaration, so the refusal is the agent's repair instruction.

title: Find every service built from a component
goal: A platform engineer names every service that was built from a given component digest.

title: Ship a component fix without a compiler release
goal: A fixed component reaches consumers without a new compiler version.
notes: Decision of 2026-10-27: one signed compiler holds every generator. A fix reaches consumers through per-component digests and a registry pin that moves apart from the compiler pin, not through a separately released generator.

title: Learn that a pinned component is superseded
goal: A service author finds out, while working, that a component the service pins has been superseded.
notes: The lifecycle records are read from the registry's current head, not from the pinned snapshot, so a consumer on an old snapshot still learns of a supersession.

title: Withdraw a component digest
goal: A component digest that must not be used any more stops being usable, and every affected service is named first.

title: Qualify a compiler release
goal: A release is qualified at an exact commit before anyone can install it.

title: Install a qualified compiler
goal: The operator installs a compiler whose identity and platform they can verify.

title: State what a service needs from the platform
goal: The platform knows, from one typed file, everything a service needs from its environment, without reading its code.
notes: Decisions of 2026-10-29: STEGO owns everything derivable from service.yaml, and the platform owns everything derivable from the environment. The Kubernetes base is a plain kustomize base; the platform's overlay supplies the image digest, namespace, replicas, PodDisruptionBudget and any change to the default resources. Every service writes platform-requirements.yaml with its secrets and configuration, backing services, network and cluster permissions. stego env check checks an environment file against it, by hand and in the platform repo's CI. The first providers are GitHub Actions and Konflux (Tekton) for CI, and Argo CD for delivery. GitHub Actions calls the platform's reusable workflow, pinned by commit; Konflux runs its standard pipeline from the generated Containerfile, and every STEGO check runs on both. Each provider names one trusted signer. The fleet stays a manual sweep: CI publishes no consumer manifest to an index.

title: Add a service rule at a slot
goal: A service rule runs at the slot it belongs to, in code the agent or author wrote and tested, and no generated file is edited by hand.
notes: Decisions of 2026-10-28: a fill belongs to one project; the compiler refuses a bound fill with no tests, or one that is not qualified; qualified means recorded test evidence and a person's key signature of that evidence, both kept in fill.yaml; a fill imports only its slot contract, the standard library and the modules the declaration lists.

title: Qualify a fill
goal: A fill ships only after its tests passed against its contract and a person signed that evidence with their own key.
notes: Decisions of 2026-10-28: a fill belongs to one project; the compiler refuses a bound fill with no tests, or one that is not qualified; qualified means recorded test evidence and a person's key signature of that evidence, both kept in fill.yaml; a fill imports only its slot contract, the standard library and the modules the declaration lists. A signature proves that a holder of a listed key signed; only a key that needs a touch, such as a hardware key, proves that a person was present, and a team may require such keys in its SIGNERS file.

title: Find an existing fill for a slot
goal: An author or an agent reuses a fill that already implements a slot, instead of writing a second one.

title: Requalify a fill after a change
goal: A fill whose code, tests or contract changed ships again only after its tests pass and a person signs the new evidence.
notes: Decisions of 2026-10-28: a fill belongs to one project; the compiler refuses a bound fill with no tests, or one that is not qualified; qualified means recorded test evidence and a person's key signature of that evidence, both kept in fill.yaml; a fill imports only its slot contract, the standard library and the modules the declaration lists.

title: Record what a service was built from
goal: The service's repo holds a record of every input its generated code came from.
notes: Decision of 2026-10-27: the record extends .stego/state.yaml, which exists wherever STEGO is used, and does not live in a second file.

title: Trust that a record matches its code
goal: A reader can trust that a service's record describes the generated code beside it.

title: Take a component fix into a service
goal: The service carries the fixed component, and the change is a diff a reviewer can read.
notes: Decision of 2026-10-27: a fix reaches a service as a pin bump and a new generation run, never as a hand edit, because a regenerated diff is auditable and a hand edit is not. Decision of 2026-10-28: Distributing owns the digest lifecycle, so its standing check runs before apply, and apply does not check standing itself. This step invokes Distributing's query, which goes outside the rule that a flow invokes its own domain's commands and queries.

title: Regenerate after a declaration change
goal: The service's generated code follows its changed declaration, and the change is a diff a reviewer can read.
notes: This is the main loop: an author or an agent changes the declaration, and a new run brings the code in line. Apply can run without a saved plan here, and then it plans in the same run.

title: Review a plan before anything changes
goal: The service author sees every file a run would change before any file changes, and apply then makes exactly those changes.
notes: Decision of 2026-10-28: a plan can be saved, under .stego/ as local working state that is not committed. Apply carries out a saved plan exactly, and can also run without one.

title: Recover from an interrupted apply
goal: After an apply stops part way, the generated files and the record agree again, and no hand-written change is lost.

title: Capture a frontend build as an input
goal: A service's frontend build becomes one checked input that generation reads, so generated code depends on no build folder or download.
notes: Decision of 2026-10-28: capturing browser assets is an input capture for Generating, like the proto files a generator reads.

title: Write a component
goal: The platform engineer adds a part that every service can build from, and makes each accidental decision once.

title: Compose a registry for a team
goal: A team may add parts of its own without weakening the parts everyone shares.

title: Curate an archetype
goal: A service author selects one archetype and gets a shape that works, with every port answered.

title: Introduce an experimental component
goal: A team may run ahead of the platform team, visibly and for a stated time, without reaching a golden path.
notes: The acceptance by name belongs to the Declaring domain: a declaration accepts an experimental component, and checking a declaration refuses one it does not accept. This use case only makes the component reachable on purpose.

title: Graduate or retire a component
goal: An experiment either becomes a part everyone can rely on, or it goes, and nobody is surprised either way.
notes: Which services use a component is recorded by the Distributing domain. Supplying holds it in a read model of its own, which that domain's published events must feed. A missed sunset fails checking in the Declaring domain, because an acceptance there cannot outlive the component.

title: Contribute a component upstream
goal: A team that solved a shared problem in its local registry gives the solution to every team, and the common registry trusts it only after the platform team's review and the quality bar.
notes: Decision of 2026-10-28: STEGO is a flywheel; consumer teams find accidental complexity and contribute components upstream (ST-BO02).
